We instantiate ZPRL on flow-matching policies and evaluate it on eight simulation tasks and four real-world tasks. Across diverse manipulation settings, ZPRL improves sample efficiency with competitive or better final performance. In the real world, ZPRL improves the average success rate on four tasks by 33.7 percentage points over imitation base policies. Our qualitative and quantitative results also indicate that ZPRL combines task success with smooth actions without explicit temporal filtering or smoothness regularization. These results suggest that a compact, task-aligned bottleneck latent provides an effective interface for online RL adaptation. Videos and code can be found at https://manutdmoon.github.io/ZPRL/.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: ALAM: Algebraically Consistent Latent Action Model for Vision-Language-Action Models
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zuojin Tang, Haoyun Liu, Xinyuan Chang, Changjie Wu, Dongjie Huo
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: ALAM introduces an Algebraically Consistent Latent Action Model that enhances vision-language-action models by leveraging structured latent transitions from action-free videos, significantly improving policy performance.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models remain constrained by the scarcity of action-labeled robot data, whereas action-free videos provide abundant evidence of how the physical world changes. Latent action models offer a promising way to extract such priors from videos, but reconstruction-trained latent codes are not necessarily suitable for policy generation: they may predict future observations while lacking the structure needed to be reused or generated coherently with robot actions. We introduce ALAM (Algebraic Latent Action Model), an Algebraically Consistent Latent Action Model that turns temporal relations in action-free video into structural supervision. Given frame triplets, ALAM learns latent transitions that are grounded by reconstruction while being regularized by composition and reversal consistency, encouraging a locally additive transition space. For downstream VLA learning, we freeze the pretrained encoder and use its latent transition sequences as auxiliary generative targets, co-generated with robot actions under a joint flow-matching objective. This couples structured latent transitions with flow-based policy generation, allowing the policy to exploit ALAM's locally consistent transition geometry without requiring latent-to-action decoding. Representation probes show that ALAM reduces additivity and reversibility errors by 25-85 times over unstructured latent-action baselines and improves long-horizon cumulative reconstruction. When transferred to VLA policies, ALAM raises the average success rate from 47.9% to 85.0% on MetaWorld MT50 and from 94.2% to 98.1% on LIBERO, with consistent gains on real-world manipulation tasks. Ablations further confirm that the strongest improvements arise from the synergy between algebraically structured latent transitions and joint flow matching. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Mark-zjtang/ALAM/tree/main.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: HuMI: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Humanoid-Free Demonstrations
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Ruiqian Nai, Boyuan Zheng, Junming Zhao, Haodong Zhu, Sicong Dai
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: HuMI is a portable framework that enhances humanoid whole-body manipulation by efficiently learning from humanoid-free demonstrations, achieving significant improvements in data collection and task success rates.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Current approaches for humanoid whole-body manipulation, primarily relying on teleoperation or visual sim-to-real reinforcement learning, are hindered by hardware logistics and complex reward engineering. Consequently, demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments. In this paper, we present the Humanoid Manipulation Interface (HuMI), a portable and efficient framework for learning diverse whole-body manipulation tasks across various environments. HuMI enables humanoid-free data collection by capturing rich whole-body motion using portable hardware. This data drives a hierarchical learning pipeline that translates human motions into dexterous and feasible humanoid skills. Extensive experiments across five whole-body tasks--including kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual manipulation--demonstrate that HuMI achieves a 3x increase in data collection efficiency compared to teleoperation and attains a 70% success rate in unseen environments.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Haozhen Zhang, Bohan Liu, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Haodong Yue
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: HiVe-Mem enhances multimodal agents' memory by interleaving horizontal expansion and vertical evidence composition, improving retrieval efficiency and task performance while minimizing token usage.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zihan Gao, Yufei Liu, Yuhong Zhang, Zhen Yu, Xinhao Huang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: HandMimicX presents an object-centric framework for learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric videos, enhancing skill transfer and promoting anatomically natural hand interactions.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from human videos remains an open challenge, particularly in the context of transferring a single demonstration into a spatially generalizable robotic skill and maintaining physically plausible human-like interactions. Unlike prior works that emphasize hand-motion imitation, we introduce an object-centric framework for acquiring dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos. Within our framework, we formulate the reinforcement learning (RL) objective in terms of object motion to decouple the underlying skill from the specific hand trajectory and impose constraints on hand-object interaction states to promote more anatomically natural hand configurations. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate that our method enables efficient learning from human videos and generalizable skill transfer across novel spatial configurations.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: AssemState: Manual and Physical-State-Guided Reasoning for Zero-shot Furniture Assembly
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zhiyuan Qi, Jierui Li, Yifan Shen, Cheng Qian, Jiateng Liu
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: AssemState enhances zero-shot furniture assembly by integrating manual guidance and physical-state reasoning, significantly improving operation recovery and pose accuracy despite persistent spatial reasoning challenges.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made significant progress in visual understanding, but precise 3D spatial reasoning integrated with physical environment remains difficult. Furniture assembly requires not only recovering step-level operations from diagrammatic manuals, but also translating semantic attachment relations into 6D pose updates that enable parts to physically interact with the environment and previously assembled components. To study this problem, we propose AssemState, a zero-shot framework for manual and physical-state-guided furniture assembly. It firstly employs anchor-guided boundary assembly states to decompose manual pages into single-part operations and recover an assembly-tree. Then, it uses iterative after-state feedback refinement to guide successive (SE(3)) updates and corrections, and validates their physical plausibility through simulation-based release tests. Experiments show that compared with the strongest prior baseline, AssemState improves F1 from 38.58\% to 62.80\% and Tree Exact Match from 28.24\% to 53.92\% for assembly-tree recovery. On 243 independently evaluated part-level operations, our proposed iterative refinement improves judge-accepted operations from 0 to 5.3\% and reduces mean Chamfer distance from 5.4111 to 1.7744. However, visually plausible candidate poses may still suffer from collision, floating, mirror-orientation errors, incomplete seating, and wrong-side attachment. These results show that AssemState improves operation-structure recovery and selected local pose metrics, while MLLMs remain limited for spatial relationship reasoning.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Zixiang Ai, Zhenyu Cui, Xu Zou, Jiahuan Zhou
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The 3R-Adapter enhances 3D reconstruction models' adaptation to challenging scenarios through a novel approach combining retrieval, rewiring, and refinement of relational structures.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have demonstrated strong generalization under large-scale pre-training, yet they struggle in long-tail scenarios such as low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation. We observe relational attention structure collapse, manifested as the failure of cross-view correspondences, as a primary cause of these limitations. While adaptation offers a practical way to bridge this gap, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches mainly perform channel-wise feature adjustment and lack mechanisms to explicitly adapt relational structures, leaving correspondence failures unresolved. In this work, we formulate adaptation of 3D reconstruction models as a problem of correspondence recovery under domain shift and propose 3R-Adapter, a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios. Our method consists of three components: Deformable Retrieval for task-adaptive relation candidate retrieval, Relational Rewiring for reconstructing cross-view relational structures, and Consistency Refinement for injecting the rewired relations into stable predictions. Extensive experiments on low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves robustness over existing PEFT methods while maintaining efficient lightweight adaptation. Our code is released at https://github.com/PKU-OV3-LAB/3R-Adapter.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Reaching Is Not Finding: Map-Anchored Visual Prompting for the Last Mile of Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Ningbo Li, Kebin Liu, Jingcan Chen, Weichen Zhang, Rong Ding
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper introduces MAP-VP, a module that enhances aerial vision-language navigation by improving object identification relative to landmarks, significantly boosting success rates without retraining.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) asks a drone to find an object described in natural language. The description usually locates the object relative to named landmarks, such as streets and buildings. We observe that current navigators often bring the drone close to the target and then stop at the wrong place: they reach the target without finding it. This gap is shared by navigators of very different designs, from imitation learners to a fine-tuned 7B vision-language model. A simple test reveals the cause. When we replace the target object in the instruction with another one next to the same landmarks, no navigator goes to it, and most stop where they did before. Navigators learn to reach the landmarks, not to identify the described object. We therefore propose MAP-VP, a plug-and-play module for the last step. After any navigator stops, MAP-VP draws the landmarks named in the instruction onto the drone's current view, using the landmark outlines that the benchmark provides on a map. A fine-tuned 4B vision-language model then locates the target relative to these landmarks. The training data are generated automatically from the benchmark annotations. Neither drawing the landmarks nor fine-tuning helps much alone, but together they are highly effective. Without retraining any navigator, MAP-VP significantly improves all six navigators we test on CityNav. It roughly doubles the success rate of the two strongest trained navigators, raising HETT from 25.9% to 54.6% and FlightGPT from 24.2% to 48.9%, whereas CityNav's official detector-based last step adds less than two points to HETT.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: BAT-WAM: Bridging Action and Touch in World-Action Models for Dexterous Hands
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Dong Fang, Feixuan Huang, Yuanxin Zhong, Yuxiang Gao, Qi Song
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: BAT-WAM is a novel framework that enhances dexterous manipulation by integrating visual, joint-state, and tactile information, significantly improving tactile reconstruction and prediction accuracy.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Dexterous manipulation with world action models (WAMs) relies on hand configuration and contact information, yet joint-state and whole-hand tactile observations may be partially or entirely missing. RGB images provide scene context and hand-object geometry but are insufficient to reliably recover these missing modalities. We further observe a correlation between hand state and tactile information. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BAT-WAM, a framework that bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations for WAMs. BAT-WAM learns separate codebooks and decoders for the tactile and action streams. An RGB-conditioned continuous latent bridge connects the two streams for bidirectional learning, while visual information serves as continuous context. Under the HTBench evaluation protocol, BAT-WAM reduces the root mean squared error (RMSE) of tactile reconstruction by 34.73% under fully masked conditions and 38.84% under partially masked conditions, relative to an image-conditioned HandTouch checkpoint. For future tactile prediction conditioned on target-time RGB and historical actions, it reduces mean RMSE by 85.56% relative to OpenWAM with HandTouch. Real-robot experiments further show that BAT-WAM consistently outperforms related WAM baselines in dexterous manipulation. Generalization experiments on unseen objects and scenes also demonstrate substantial improvements over baseline models. These findings support joint modeling of visual context, hand state, and touch as a representation approach for multimodal WAMs.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Robotic Spatiotemporal Editing: A Unified Interface for Controllable Action Generation via Masked Action Reconstruction
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yanbang Li, Bu He, Yi Tian, Yu-Chiao Huang, Chenyu Zhang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper presents the MAP interface for controllable robot action generation through spatiotemporal references, achieving high task success rates and reduced control errors in real-world applications.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Generative policies can synthesize robot behaviors, yet controlling and editing them through diverse spatiotemporal references remains challenging. In the real world, human intent requires robot behaviors that satisfy constraints on where, when, and how actions are executed. Our key insight is that spatiotemporal control references, such as keypoints, flows, orientations, and keyposes, can be viewed as partial specifications of the same temporal Cartesian action space. We introduce the MAP (Masked Action Space) interface to unify these action references and formulate controllable manipulation as an action inpainting problem. Our Inpainting Policy (IP) reconstructs missing action dimensions of the end-effector, combining progress-guided alignment with multi-mask training supporting unseen action-constraint combinations. We further adopt a training-free RePaint variant that iteratively inpaints the action during denoising to reduce control error. On ManiSkill and LIBERO-10, our policy achieves average task success rates of 92.67% and 64.67%, respectively.Real-world experiments demonstrate spatiotemporal control with average positional and rotational errors of 44.3 mm and 7°, respectively, showing that our policy can use diverse references to guide executable robot behaviors.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: RefRef: A Dataset and Benchmark for Reconstructing Refractive and Reflective Objects
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Yue Yin, Enze Tao, Weijian Deng, Dylan Campbell
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The RefRef dataset introduces 210 diverse scenes for benchmarking 3D reconstruction of refractive and reflective objects, addressing limitations in current methods and datasets.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Modern 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis approaches have demonstrated strong performance on scenes with opaque, non-refractive objects. However, most assume straight light paths and therefore cannot properly handle refractive and reflective materials. The lack of datasets specialized for these effects has impeded efforts to fairly and thoroughly evaluate performance and thereby make progress in this domain. Most existing datasets focus on opaque scenes, while those targeting refractive objects are often limited to thin glass with negligible ray bending, untinted single-material objects, or backgrounds treated as infinitely-distant, leaving key failure modes under strong refraction untested. To address this gap, we introduce the RefRef dataset. It contains 150 synthetic and 60 real scenes spanning varying levels of geometric complexity and diverse background types that expose the limitations of existing methods. For the purpose of benchmarking, we also provide an oracle method that, given the object geometry and refractive indices, calculates accurate light paths for neural rendering, and a simple two-stage baseline that relaxes these assumptions. We evaluate these against state-of-the-art methods and show that the task is far from solved.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: S2HAND: Accuracy-Preservation Trade-Offs for Hand Specialization in Whole-Body Pose Models
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Singyu Muk, Xuanren Song, Kalin Stefanov
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: S2HAND introduces a specialized framework for whole-body pose estimation that enhances hand accuracy while managing trade-offs in preservation and performance across multiple benchmarks.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Unified whole-body pose estimators jointly predict body, face, and hand landmarks, but often degrade on small, blurred, or occluded hands. Attaching a standalone hand specialist introduces extra detection overhead, coordinate alignment, and wrist-stitching artifacts. We introduce S2HAND, a hand-specialized Sapiens2-5B framework that preserves the native 308-keypoint output interface. Specifically, S2HAND-MT adapts a lightweight 0.87M-parameter pose branch to route 40 finger heatmaps while strictly preserving the shared Transformer, auxiliary task heads, and the other 268 body, foot, and face heatmaps. S2HAND-Pose further fine-tunes three Fisher-selected Transformer blocks (267.13M parameters), trading exact preservation for stronger hand recovery: it lifts macro AUC from 57.83% to 65.73% across HInt TEST, COCO WholeBody VAL, and FreiHAND EVAL, and surpasses HInt-adapted Hand5/HRNet and stitched Hand5 systems on all five Native Pipeline benchmarks. On COCO, S2HAND-Pose improves hand AP by 12.89 points and body-plus-foot AP by 0.19 points. Across a 512-image multi-task audit, it maintains 99.60% foreground segmentation agreement with the public checkpoint, with quantified normal and pointmap drift. Its 2D coordinates also lower 3D mesh error in frozen Pose2Mesh transfer, while our optional TailGuard re-cropping module cuts S2HAND-MT's severe failure rate on NewDays from 13.45% to 10.43%. S2HAND thus resolves the whole-body hand bottleneck with either exact non-hand preservation (MT) or empirically audited trade-offs (Pose).

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: DAC-MACE: Context-Conditioned Expert Routing for Compact Scene Coordinate Regression in Camera Relocalization
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Dingying Fan, Mingkai Liu, Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Xianliang Huang
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: DAC-MACE improves camera relocalization by enhancing expert routing through contextualized features, achieving the lowest translation error among RGB-only scene coordinate regression methods.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: A camera becomes an absolute pose sensor when its images can be relocalized against a prebuilt map of the scene. On mobile robots and augmented-reality devices, that map must be small and quick to build. Scene coordinate regression (SCR) stores the scene in a compact network that predicts a 3D coordinate for every pixel, and mixture-of-experts (MoE) variants extend its capacity to larger outdoor scenes. In existing MoE-based SCR, however, the router assigns each pixel to an expert from the same local descriptor that the experts regress from, so repeated facades and windows at different locations receive similar routing inputs. We present DAC-MACE, which conditions soft expert routing on recalibrated and contextualized features. A residual context adapter (RCA) reweights the channels and locations of frozen encoder features, a global context encoder (GCE) mixes them with multi-scale self-attention, and an image-level pooled descriptor is added to the router input. A dual-threshold RANSAC--Levenberg--Marquardt estimator recovers the pose. On Cambridge Landmarks, DAC-MACE attains a mean per-scene median translation error of 13.0 cm over three seeds, the lowest among the RGB-only SCR methods compared (GLACE 13.6 cm, MACE 14.4 cm), and reduces the error on the largest scene from 24 to 19 cm relative to MACE. In a cumulative study, the MoE head, GCE, RCA, and the dual-threshold estimator lower the mean error from 17.0 cm to 14.4, 14.0, 13.6, and 13.0 cm. On 7-Scenes, adding GCE to a single ACE head raises Recall@(5 cm, 5$^\circ$) from 86.56% to 87.60%.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Haoming Wang, Yongjian Fu, Ju Ren, Wei Gao
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: WorldMind enhances visual spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models by enabling active latent world simulation, achieving significant performance improvements without relying on pixel generation.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have continuous deficiency in spatial reasoning tasks that require \emph{mental spatial transformation}, such as reasoning under hypothetical changes in viewpoint or position, known as perspective-taking tasks. Existing approaches either scale linguistic reasoning or augment VLMs with static geometric representations, but neither directly enables active transformation of the represented scene. World models offer this capability, yet existing systems typically communicate through synthesized RGB images, introducing a latent-to-pixel-to-latent bottleneck. We introduce \emph{WorldMind}, a framework for test-time scaling of spatial reasoning through latent world simulation. Given a query and observation, the VLM selects useful spatial transformations, while a world model executes them and exposes aligned intermediate latent features directly to the VLM. The resulting latent evidence is incorporated into subsequent reasoning steps, enabling iterative spatial simulation without repeatedly decoding imagined states into pixels. To optimize this interaction, WorldMind further employs process-verifiable reinforcement learning that rewards reasoning progress only when the associated action and latent transition are valid. WorldMind thus scales spatial reasoning by allocating additional inference-time computation to active world simulation rather than generating more language or pixels. Across VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench, and MindCube-Tiny, WorldMind achieves an average improvement of 16.0% over the base VLM and 8.3% over the strongest RGB-based world simulation.

具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).title: Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization for On-Policy Reasoning Distillation under Large Policy Divergence
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).authors_text: Xinyu Liu, Kechen Jiao, Chunyang Xiao, Runsong Zhao, Junhao Ruan
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).summary: The paper introduces Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO), enhancing on-policy reasoning distillation by effectively guiding exploration under large policy divergence, outperforming traditional methods.
具身智能实验室 (TEA Lab).debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has become a promising paradigm for reasoning-oriented post-training of large language models (LLMs), especially when combined with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR). Existing OPD methods rely on reverse KL (RKL)-based teacher supervision over trajectories sampled from the student policy. However, we identify a critical limitation: under large teacher--student policy divergence, RL-driven exploration often produces trajectories outside the teacher distribution, resulting in uninformative negative feedback. To address this, we propose Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO), an on-policy reasoning distillation method that remains effective under large policy divergence settings. Rather than relying solely on evaluative supervision, TGPO uses teacher to directly guide token level generation conditioning on student-generated contexts; together with RLVR-style trajectory level rewards, TGPO steers exploration toward improved continuations. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that TGPO consistently outperforms existing RKL-based OPD methods and remains robust across different teacher models.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yuguang Yang, Zhewen Tan, Canyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Cheng Chi
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: AutoVLA-D enhances autonomous driving trajectory prediction by introducing a discrete trajectory-geometric condition, improving performance through a two-stage learning framework.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Autoregressive VLA planning usually predicts continuous trajectories as the final output, but driving instructions often describe actions rather than ego states, which weakens direct conditioning on the final continuous trajectory. We address this gap with TrajCond, which introduces a discrete trajectory-geometric condition for VLA planning. Specifically, we represent TrajCond as a 1D-Brohan differential action trajectory and learn it with a two-stage training framework before final continuous trajectory prediction. With the simultaneous autoregressive generation of discrete and numeric trajectories, we name our method AutoVLA-D (Double). Experiments on NAVSIM navtest, nuScenes, and NeuroNCAP show that discrete trajectories are weaker as direct outputs but more effective as TrajCond, consistently improving final continuous trajectory prediction across closed-loop and open-loop driving benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/ShivaTeam/AutoVLA-D.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Jinghe Wang, Xinrui Cao, Duo Wu, Chenghao Gu, Yong Zhong
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: GeoMind is a new benchmark for evaluating spatial understanding in robotic manipulation, focusing on spatial reasoning and memory through diverse, automated tabletop tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation has advanced rapidly in mapping visual observations and language instructions to actions. However, reliable manipulation in open-world environments requires robust spatial understanding: the ability to identify targets in complex layouts (spatial reasoning) and adapt to scenes that continuously evolve through interaction (spatial memory). Yet existing embodied benchmarks fall short in evaluating spatial understanding: they often introduce strong visual cues that bypass spatial reasoning, and focus on static scenes that offer little insight into an agent's capacity for spatial memory. To address this gap, we introduce GeoMind, a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation. GeoMind comprises 54 evaluated task variants organized around spatial reasoning and spatial memory. It also incorporates a scalable pipeline that automates the generation and annotation of task instances with verified targets and executable interactions. Extensive evaluations across diverse embodied agents reveal their consistent weaknesses in spatial understanding. Our findings highlight that these agents struggle to track identities after spatial changes and convert relational or geometric constraints into executable actions. We release the GeoMind benchmark at https://github.com/Notfound-JH/GEOMIND-benchmark.git.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Lei Shu, Zizhou Huang, Yunuo Chen, Yifei Li, Tao Du
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: This paper categorizes differentiable physics simulation methods, clarifying derivative sources, implementation impacts on accuracy, and explores gradient utility across various applications and challenges.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The model classes, systems techniques and applications are surveyed through this lens, and we close with a reporting checklist, a released diagnostic that computes it, and a research agenda.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Autonomous Precision Milling of Biological Structures via Generic Anatomical Priors and Active Boundary Perception
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Enduo Zhao, Xiaofeng Lin, Yifan Wang, Yuhan Song, Weihan Li
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: This paper presents a state-adaptive framework for autonomous precision milling of biological structures, integrating generic anatomical priors with active boundary perception for improved accuracy and adaptability.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Autonomous precision milling of biological structures is challenged by incomplete knowledge of target geometry, local material thickness, and critical internal boundaries. Subject-specific preoperative models can address geometric and thickness variations, but static models cannot determine boundary status encountered during execution, while repeated target-specific imaging limits scalability. This article presents a state-adaptive autonomous milling framework that assigns complementary roles to generic anatomical priors and active boundary perception. A generic anatomical prior provides conservative global guidance and is transformed through semantic-guided registration and hybrid vision-force calibration into robot-executable guidance for individual targets. As milling approaches uncertain boundaries, the robot actively probes the remaining structure and uses relative stiffness changes to estimate boundary status and structural detachability. A state-adaptive controller governs transitions between active perception and spatially selective incremental refinement, repeating this cycle until the termination criterion is satisfied. Hierarchical experiments on biological surrogates and in vivo mouse cranial window creation demonstrate accurate anatomical prior transfer, reliable boundary adaptation, and autonomous precision milling of biological structures.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yitian Pang, Yifan Li, Xiaowei Yue, Li Zheng
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: GOPR-CAD introduces a novel Text-to-CAD pipeline using Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning to enhance structural fidelity in CAD model generation, achieving high structural yields.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: RoadState: A Domain-Prior-Enhanced Vision-Language System for Industrial-Grade Lane-Level Map Updating
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Deguo Xia, Zihan Li, Jiaqi Wang, Dong Xie, Xiyan Liu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: RoadState is a vision-language system that enhances lane-level map updating through autoregressive state estimation and domain-prior reasoning, achieving high accuracy and cost reduction in real-world applications.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Lane-level map updating requires temporally consistent, physically valid, and auditable road-scene semantics despite occlusions, ambiguous lane markings, temporary obstacles, and viewpoint changes. We present RoadState, a production-deployed vision-language system that transforms sequential road-scene observations into structured lane-level semantics for Baidu Maps' map-updating pipeline. Its core model, RoadState-VLM, formulates road-scene understanding as autoregressive state estimation, predicting the current structured road state from the previous observation and symbolic state together with the current observation. We introduce Geometric Chain-of-Thought (Geo-CoT), which uses a directed acyclic graph of semantic dependencies as a domain prior to improve semantic consistency and reasoning fidelity across interdependent road-state dimensions. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset show that RoadState-VLM achieves 94.33% mean accuracy across six road-state dimensions, outperforming the strongest fine-tuned VLM baseline. Ablation studies further demonstrate the complementary effectiveness of Geo-CoT and temporal transition context. A cascaded routing pipeline directs routine cases to lightweight models while reserving complex cases for RoadState-VLM. Since its deployment in March 2025, RoadState has supported lane-level map updating across more than 360 cities and reduced overall production costs by 30%. Together with human-in-the-loop auditing, the system maintains robust performance under stress-test conditions. These results demonstrate how domain-prior-enhanced reasoning, structured state interfaces, selective routing, and human quality control can bridge the gap between VLM-based road-scene understanding and large-scale lane-level map updating.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Beyond Action Residuals: Real-World Robot Policy Steering via Bottleneck Latent Reinforcement Learning
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Dongjie Yu, Kun Lei, Zhennan Jiang, Jia Pan, Huazhe Xu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper presents Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), which enhances pretrained robot policies through a compact bottleneck latent interface, improving adaptation and performance in real-world tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Pretrained imitation policies have become a strong foundation for robot manipulation, but online adaptation can further improve policy performance within their pretrained behavioral support. A central question is therefore how reinforcement learning (RL) should adapt policies after offline pretraining. Existing lightweight methods commonly apply residual corrections directly in action space. We investigate how the steering interface affects online RL. In this work, we propose Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), an approach that steers pretrained policies through a compact bottleneck latent rather than through policy weights or output actions. Building on an offline-learned bottleneck policy interface introduced by previous work, ZPRL turns this representation into an online RL control space through reward-driven residual perturbations while freezing the pretrained policy. We instantiate ZPRL on flow-matching policies and evaluate it on eight simulation tasks and four real-world tasks. Across diverse manipulation settings, ZPRL improves sample efficiency with competitive or better final performance. In the real world, ZPRL improves the average success rate on four tasks by 33.7 percentage points over imitation base policies. Our qualitative and quantitative results also indicate that ZPRL combines task success with smooth actions without explicit temporal filtering or smoothness regularization. These results suggest that a compact, task-aligned bottleneck latent provides an effective interface for online RL adaptation. Videos and code can be found at https://manutdmoon.github.io/ZPRL/.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: ALAM: Algebraically Consistent Latent Action Model for Vision-Language-Action Models
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zuojin Tang, Haoyun Liu, Xinyuan Chang, Changjie Wu, Dongjie Huo
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: ALAM introduces an Algebraically Consistent Latent Action Model that enhances vision-language-action models by leveraging structured latent transitions from action-free videos, significantly improving policy performance.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models remain constrained by the scarcity of action-labeled robot data, whereas action-free videos provide abundant evidence of how the physical world changes. Latent action models offer a promising way to extract such priors from videos, but reconstruction-trained latent codes are not necessarily suitable for policy generation: they may predict future observations while lacking the structure needed to be reused or generated coherently with robot actions. We introduce ALAM (Algebraic Latent Action Model), an Algebraically Consistent Latent Action Model that turns temporal relations in action-free video into structural supervision. Given frame triplets, ALAM learns latent transitions that are grounded by reconstruction while being regularized by composition and reversal consistency, encouraging a locally additive transition space. For downstream VLA learning, we freeze the pretrained encoder and use its latent transition sequences as auxiliary generative targets, co-generated with robot actions under a joint flow-matching objective. This couples structured latent transitions with flow-based policy generation, allowing the policy to exploit ALAM's locally consistent transition geometry without requiring latent-to-action decoding. Representation probes show that ALAM reduces additivity and reversibility errors by 25-85 times over unstructured latent-action baselines and improves long-horizon cumulative reconstruction. When transferred to VLA policies, ALAM raises the average success rate from 47.9% to 85.0% on MetaWorld MT50 and from 94.2% to 98.1% on LIBERO, with consistent gains on real-world manipulation tasks. Ablations further confirm that the strongest improvements arise from the synergy between algebraically structured latent transitions and joint flow matching. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Mark-zjtang/ALAM/tree/main.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: HuMI: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Humanoid-Free Demonstrations
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Ruiqian Nai, Boyuan Zheng, Junming Zhao, Haodong Zhu, Sicong Dai
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: HuMI is a portable framework that enhances humanoid whole-body manipulation by efficiently learning from humanoid-free demonstrations, achieving significant improvements in data collection and task success rates.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Current approaches for humanoid whole-body manipulation, primarily relying on teleoperation or visual sim-to-real reinforcement learning, are hindered by hardware logistics and complex reward engineering. Consequently, demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments. In this paper, we present the Humanoid Manipulation Interface (HuMI), a portable and efficient framework for learning diverse whole-body manipulation tasks across various environments. HuMI enables humanoid-free data collection by capturing rich whole-body motion using portable hardware. This data drives a hierarchical learning pipeline that translates human motions into dexterous and feasible humanoid skills. Extensive experiments across five whole-body tasks--including kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual manipulation--demonstrate that HuMI achieves a 3x increase in data collection efficiency compared to teleoperation and attains a 70% success rate in unseen environments.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Haozhen Zhang, Bohan Liu, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Haodong Yue
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: HiVe-Mem enhances multimodal agents' memory by interleaving horizontal expansion and vertical evidence composition, improving retrieval efficiency and task performance while minimizing token usage.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zihan Gao, Yufei Liu, Yuhong Zhang, Zhen Yu, Xinhao Huang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: HandMimicX presents an object-centric framework for learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric videos, enhancing skill transfer and promoting anatomically natural hand interactions.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from human videos remains an open challenge, particularly in the context of transferring a single demonstration into a spatially generalizable robotic skill and maintaining physically plausible human-like interactions. Unlike prior works that emphasize hand-motion imitation, we introduce an object-centric framework for acquiring dexterous skills from egocentric human RGB-D videos. Within our framework, we formulate the reinforcement learning (RL) objective in terms of object motion to decouple the underlying skill from the specific hand trajectory and impose constraints on hand-object interaction states to promote more anatomically natural hand configurations. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate that our method enables efficient learning from human videos and generalizable skill transfer across novel spatial configurations.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: AssemState: Manual and Physical-State-Guided Reasoning for Zero-shot Furniture Assembly
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zhiyuan Qi, Jierui Li, Yifan Shen, Cheng Qian, Jiateng Liu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: AssemState enhances zero-shot furniture assembly by integrating manual guidance and physical-state reasoning, significantly improving operation recovery and pose accuracy despite persistent spatial reasoning challenges.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made significant progress in visual understanding, but precise 3D spatial reasoning integrated with physical environment remains difficult. Furniture assembly requires not only recovering step-level operations from diagrammatic manuals, but also translating semantic attachment relations into 6D pose updates that enable parts to physically interact with the environment and previously assembled components. To study this problem, we propose AssemState, a zero-shot framework for manual and physical-state-guided furniture assembly. It firstly employs anchor-guided boundary assembly states to decompose manual pages into single-part operations and recover an assembly-tree. Then, it uses iterative after-state feedback refinement to guide successive (SE(3)) updates and corrections, and validates their physical plausibility through simulation-based release tests. Experiments show that compared with the strongest prior baseline, AssemState improves F1 from 38.58\% to 62.80\% and Tree Exact Match from 28.24\% to 53.92\% for assembly-tree recovery. On 243 independently evaluated part-level operations, our proposed iterative refinement improves judge-accepted operations from 0 to 5.3\% and reduces mean Chamfer distance from 5.4111 to 1.7744. However, visually plausible candidate poses may still suffer from collision, floating, mirror-orientation errors, incomplete seating, and wrong-side attachment. These results show that AssemState improves operation-structure recovery and selected local pose metrics, while MLLMs remain limited for spatial relationship reasoning.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zixiang Ai, Zhenyu Cui, Xu Zou, Jiahuan Zhou
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The 3R-Adapter enhances 3D reconstruction models' adaptation to challenging scenarios through a novel approach combining retrieval, rewiring, and refinement of relational structures.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have demonstrated strong generalization under large-scale pre-training, yet they struggle in long-tail scenarios such as low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation. We observe relational attention structure collapse, manifested as the failure of cross-view correspondences, as a primary cause of these limitations. While adaptation offers a practical way to bridge this gap, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches mainly perform channel-wise feature adjustment and lack mechanisms to explicitly adapt relational structures, leaving correspondence failures unresolved. In this work, we formulate adaptation of 3D reconstruction models as a problem of correspondence recovery under domain shift and propose 3R-Adapter, a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios. Our method consists of three components: Deformable Retrieval for task-adaptive relation candidate retrieval, Relational Rewiring for reconstructing cross-view relational structures, and Consistency Refinement for injecting the rewired relations into stable predictions. Extensive experiments on low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves robustness over existing PEFT methods while maintaining efficient lightweight adaptation. Our code is released at https://github.com/PKU-OV3-LAB/3R-Adapter.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Reaching Is Not Finding: Map-Anchored Visual Prompting for the Last Mile of Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Ningbo Li, Kebin Liu, Jingcan Chen, Weichen Zhang, Rong Ding
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper introduces MAP-VP, a module that enhances aerial vision-language navigation by improving object identification relative to landmarks, significantly boosting success rates without retraining.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) asks a drone to find an object described in natural language. The description usually locates the object relative to named landmarks, such as streets and buildings. We observe that current navigators often bring the drone close to the target and then stop at the wrong place: they reach the target without finding it. This gap is shared by navigators of very different designs, from imitation learners to a fine-tuned 7B vision-language model. A simple test reveals the cause. When we replace the target object in the instruction with another one next to the same landmarks, no navigator goes to it, and most stop where they did before. Navigators learn to reach the landmarks, not to identify the described object. We therefore propose MAP-VP, a plug-and-play module for the last step. After any navigator stops, MAP-VP draws the landmarks named in the instruction onto the drone's current view, using the landmark outlines that the benchmark provides on a map. A fine-tuned 4B vision-language model then locates the target relative to these landmarks. The training data are generated automatically from the benchmark annotations. Neither drawing the landmarks nor fine-tuning helps much alone, but together they are highly effective. Without retraining any navigator, MAP-VP significantly improves all six navigators we test on CityNav. It roughly doubles the success rate of the two strongest trained navigators, raising HETT from 25.9% to 54.6% and FlightGPT from 24.2% to 48.9%, whereas CityNav's official detector-based last step adds less than two points to HETT.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: BAT-WAM: Bridging Action and Touch in World-Action Models for Dexterous Hands
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Dong Fang, Feixuan Huang, Yuanxin Zhong, Yuxiang Gao, Qi Song
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: BAT-WAM is a novel framework that enhances dexterous manipulation by integrating visual, joint-state, and tactile information, significantly improving tactile reconstruction and prediction accuracy.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Dexterous manipulation with world action models (WAMs) relies on hand configuration and contact information, yet joint-state and whole-hand tactile observations may be partially or entirely missing. RGB images provide scene context and hand-object geometry but are insufficient to reliably recover these missing modalities. We further observe a correlation between hand state and tactile information. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BAT-WAM, a framework that bridges visual, joint-state, and tactile representations for WAMs. BAT-WAM learns separate codebooks and decoders for the tactile and action streams. An RGB-conditioned continuous latent bridge connects the two streams for bidirectional learning, while visual information serves as continuous context. Under the HTBench evaluation protocol, BAT-WAM reduces the root mean squared error (RMSE) of tactile reconstruction by 34.73% under fully masked conditions and 38.84% under partially masked conditions, relative to an image-conditioned HandTouch checkpoint. For future tactile prediction conditioned on target-time RGB and historical actions, it reduces mean RMSE by 85.56% relative to OpenWAM with HandTouch. Real-robot experiments further show that BAT-WAM consistently outperforms related WAM baselines in dexterous manipulation. Generalization experiments on unseen objects and scenes also demonstrate substantial improvements over baseline models. These findings support joint modeling of visual context, hand state, and touch as a representation approach for multimodal WAMs.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Robotic Spatiotemporal Editing: A Unified Interface for Controllable Action Generation via Masked Action Reconstruction
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yanbang Li, Bu He, Yi Tian, Yu-Chiao Huang, Chenyu Zhang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper presents the MAP interface for controllable robot action generation through spatiotemporal references, achieving high task success rates and reduced control errors in real-world applications.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Generative policies can synthesize robot behaviors, yet controlling and editing them through diverse spatiotemporal references remains challenging. In the real world, human intent requires robot behaviors that satisfy constraints on where, when, and how actions are executed. Our key insight is that spatiotemporal control references, such as keypoints, flows, orientations, and keyposes, can be viewed as partial specifications of the same temporal Cartesian action space. We introduce the MAP (Masked Action Space) interface to unify these action references and formulate controllable manipulation as an action inpainting problem. Our Inpainting Policy (IP) reconstructs missing action dimensions of the end-effector, combining progress-guided alignment with multi-mask training supporting unseen action-constraint combinations. We further adopt a training-free RePaint variant that iteratively inpaints the action during denoising to reduce control error. On ManiSkill and LIBERO-10, our policy achieves average task success rates of 92.67% and 64.67%, respectively.Real-world experiments demonstrate spatiotemporal control with average positional and rotational errors of 44.3 mm and 7°, respectively, showing that our policy can use diverse references to guide executable robot behaviors.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: RefRef: A Dataset and Benchmark for Reconstructing Refractive and Reflective Objects
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yue Yin, Enze Tao, Weijian Deng, Dylan Campbell
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The RefRef dataset introduces 210 diverse scenes for benchmarking 3D reconstruction of refractive and reflective objects, addressing limitations in current methods and datasets.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Modern 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis approaches have demonstrated strong performance on scenes with opaque, non-refractive objects. However, most assume straight light paths and therefore cannot properly handle refractive and reflective materials. The lack of datasets specialized for these effects has impeded efforts to fairly and thoroughly evaluate performance and thereby make progress in this domain. Most existing datasets focus on opaque scenes, while those targeting refractive objects are often limited to thin glass with negligible ray bending, untinted single-material objects, or backgrounds treated as infinitely-distant, leaving key failure modes under strong refraction untested. To address this gap, we introduce the RefRef dataset. It contains 150 synthetic and 60 real scenes spanning varying levels of geometric complexity and diverse background types that expose the limitations of existing methods. For the purpose of benchmarking, we also provide an oracle method that, given the object geometry and refractive indices, calculates accurate light paths for neural rendering, and a simple two-stage baseline that relaxes these assumptions. We evaluate these against state-of-the-art methods and show that the task is far from solved.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: S2HAND: Accuracy-Preservation Trade-Offs for Hand Specialization in Whole-Body Pose Models
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Singyu Muk, Xuanren Song, Kalin Stefanov
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: S2HAND introduces a specialized framework for whole-body pose estimation that enhances hand accuracy while managing trade-offs in preservation and performance across multiple benchmarks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Unified whole-body pose estimators jointly predict body, face, and hand landmarks, but often degrade on small, blurred, or occluded hands. Attaching a standalone hand specialist introduces extra detection overhead, coordinate alignment, and wrist-stitching artifacts. We introduce S2HAND, a hand-specialized Sapiens2-5B framework that preserves the native 308-keypoint output interface. Specifically, S2HAND-MT adapts a lightweight 0.87M-parameter pose branch to route 40 finger heatmaps while strictly preserving the shared Transformer, auxiliary task heads, and the other 268 body, foot, and face heatmaps. S2HAND-Pose further fine-tunes three Fisher-selected Transformer blocks (267.13M parameters), trading exact preservation for stronger hand recovery: it lifts macro AUC from 57.83% to 65.73% across HInt TEST, COCO WholeBody VAL, and FreiHAND EVAL, and surpasses HInt-adapted Hand5/HRNet and stitched Hand5 systems on all five Native Pipeline benchmarks. On COCO, S2HAND-Pose improves hand AP by 12.89 points and body-plus-foot AP by 0.19 points. Across a 512-image multi-task audit, it maintains 99.60% foreground segmentation agreement with the public checkpoint, with quantified normal and pointmap drift. Its 2D coordinates also lower 3D mesh error in frozen Pose2Mesh transfer, while our optional TailGuard re-cropping module cuts S2HAND-MT's severe failure rate on NewDays from 13.45% to 10.43%. S2HAND thus resolves the whole-body hand bottleneck with either exact non-hand preservation (MT) or empirically audited trade-offs (Pose).

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: DAC-MACE: Context-Conditioned Expert Routing for Compact Scene Coordinate Regression in Camera Relocalization
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Dingying Fan, Mingkai Liu, Haohua Que, Haojia Gao, Xianliang Huang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: DAC-MACE improves camera relocalization by enhancing expert routing through contextualized features, achieving the lowest translation error among RGB-only scene coordinate regression methods.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: A camera becomes an absolute pose sensor when its images can be relocalized against a prebuilt map of the scene. On mobile robots and augmented-reality devices, that map must be small and quick to build. Scene coordinate regression (SCR) stores the scene in a compact network that predicts a 3D coordinate for every pixel, and mixture-of-experts (MoE) variants extend its capacity to larger outdoor scenes. In existing MoE-based SCR, however, the router assigns each pixel to an expert from the same local descriptor that the experts regress from, so repeated facades and windows at different locations receive similar routing inputs. We present DAC-MACE, which conditions soft expert routing on recalibrated and contextualized features. A residual context adapter (RCA) reweights the channels and locations of frozen encoder features, a global context encoder (GCE) mixes them with multi-scale self-attention, and an image-level pooled descriptor is added to the router input. A dual-threshold RANSAC--Levenberg--Marquardt estimator recovers the pose. On Cambridge Landmarks, DAC-MACE attains a mean per-scene median translation error of 13.0 cm over three seeds, the lowest among the RGB-only SCR methods compared (GLACE 13.6 cm, MACE 14.4 cm), and reduces the error on the largest scene from 24 to 19 cm relative to MACE. In a cumulative study, the MoE head, GCE, RCA, and the dual-threshold estimator lower the mean error from 17.0 cm to 14.4, 14.0, 13.6, and 13.0 cm. On 7-Scenes, adding GCE to a single ACE head raises Recall@(5 cm, 5$^\circ$) from 86.56% to 87.60%.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Haoming Wang, Yongjian Fu, Ju Ren, Wei Gao
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: WorldMind enhances visual spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models by enabling active latent world simulation, achieving significant performance improvements without relying on pixel generation.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have continuous deficiency in spatial reasoning tasks that require \emph{mental spatial transformation}, such as reasoning under hypothetical changes in viewpoint or position, known as perspective-taking tasks. Existing approaches either scale linguistic reasoning or augment VLMs with static geometric representations, but neither directly enables active transformation of the represented scene. World models offer this capability, yet existing systems typically communicate through synthesized RGB images, introducing a latent-to-pixel-to-latent bottleneck. We introduce \emph{WorldMind}, a framework for test-time scaling of spatial reasoning through latent world simulation. Given a query and observation, the VLM selects useful spatial transformations, while a world model executes them and exposes aligned intermediate latent features directly to the VLM. The resulting latent evidence is incorporated into subsequent reasoning steps, enabling iterative spatial simulation without repeatedly decoding imagined states into pixels. To optimize this interaction, WorldMind further employs process-verifiable reinforcement learning that rewards reasoning progress only when the associated action and latent transition are valid. WorldMind thus scales spatial reasoning by allocating additional inference-time computation to active world simulation rather than generating more language or pixels. Across VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench, and MindCube-Tiny, WorldMind achieves an average improvement of 16.0% over the base VLM and 8.3% over the strongest RGB-based world simulation.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization for On-Policy Reasoning Distillation under Large Policy Divergence
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xinyu Liu, Kechen Jiao, Chunyang Xiao, Runsong Zhao, Junhao Ruan
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper introduces Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO), enhancing on-policy reasoning distillation by effectively guiding exploration under large policy divergence, outperforming traditional methods.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has become a promising paradigm for reasoning-oriented post-training of large language models (LLMs), especially when combined with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR). Existing OPD methods rely on reverse KL (RKL)-based teacher supervision over trajectories sampled from the student policy. However, we identify a critical limitation: under large teacher--student policy divergence, RL-driven exploration often produces trajectories outside the teacher distribution, resulting in uninformative negative feedback. To address this, we propose Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO), an on-policy reasoning distillation method that remains effective under large policy divergence settings. Rather than relying solely on evaluative supervision, TGPO uses teacher to directly guide token level generation conditioning on student-generated contexts; together with RLVR-style trajectory level rewards, TGPO steers exploration toward improved continuations. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that TGPO consistently outperforms existing RKL-based OPD methods and remains robust across different teacher models.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yuguang Yang, Zhewen Tan, Canyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Cheng Chi
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: AutoVLA-D enhances autonomous driving trajectory prediction by introducing a discrete trajectory-geometric condition, improving performance through a two-stage learning framework.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Autoregressive VLA planning usually predicts continuous trajectories as the final output, but driving instructions often describe actions rather than ego states, which weakens direct conditioning on the final continuous trajectory. We address this gap with TrajCond, which introduces a discrete trajectory-geometric condition for VLA planning. Specifically, we represent TrajCond as a 1D-Brohan differential action trajectory and learn it with a two-stage training framework before final continuous trajectory prediction. With the simultaneous autoregressive generation of discrete and numeric trajectories, we name our method AutoVLA-D (Double). Experiments on NAVSIM navtest, nuScenes, and NeuroNCAP show that discrete trajectories are weaker as direct outputs but more effective as TrajCond, consistently improving final continuous trajectory prediction across closed-loop and open-loop driving benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/ShivaTeam/AutoVLA-D.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jinghe Wang, Xinrui Cao, Duo Wu, Chenghao Gu, Yong Zhong
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: GeoMind is a new benchmark for evaluating spatial understanding in robotic manipulation, focusing on spatial reasoning and memory through diverse, automated tabletop tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation has advanced rapidly in mapping visual observations and language instructions to actions. However, reliable manipulation in open-world environments requires robust spatial understanding: the ability to identify targets in complex layouts (spatial reasoning) and adapt to scenes that continuously evolve through interaction (spatial memory). Yet existing embodied benchmarks fall short in evaluating spatial understanding: they often introduce strong visual cues that bypass spatial reasoning, and focus on static scenes that offer little insight into an agent's capacity for spatial memory. To address this gap, we introduce GeoMind, a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation. GeoMind comprises 54 evaluated task variants organized around spatial reasoning and spatial memory. It also incorporates a scalable pipeline that automates the generation and annotation of task instances with verified targets and executable interactions. Extensive evaluations across diverse embodied agents reveal their consistent weaknesses in spatial understanding. Our findings highlight that these agents struggle to track identities after spatial changes and convert relational or geometric constraints into executable actions. We release the GeoMind benchmark at https://github.com/Notfound-JH/GEOMIND-benchmark.git.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Lei Shu, Zizhou Huang, Yunuo Chen, Yifei Li, Tao Du
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: This paper categorizes differentiable physics simulation methods, clarifying derivative sources, implementation impacts on accuracy, and explores gradient utility across various applications and challenges.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The model classes, systems techniques and applications are surveyed through this lens, and we close with a reporting checklist, a released diagnostic that computes it, and a research agenda.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Autonomous Precision Milling of Biological Structures via Generic Anatomical Priors and Active Boundary Perception
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Enduo Zhao, Xiaofeng Lin, Yifan Wang, Yuhan Song, Weihan Li
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: This paper presents a state-adaptive framework for autonomous precision milling of biological structures, integrating generic anatomical priors with active boundary perception for improved accuracy and adaptability.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Autonomous precision milling of biological structures is challenged by incomplete knowledge of target geometry, local material thickness, and critical internal boundaries. Subject-specific preoperative models can address geometric and thickness variations, but static models cannot determine boundary status encountered during execution, while repeated target-specific imaging limits scalability. This article presents a state-adaptive autonomous milling framework that assigns complementary roles to generic anatomical priors and active boundary perception. A generic anatomical prior provides conservative global guidance and is transformed through semantic-guided registration and hybrid vision-force calibration into robot-executable guidance for individual targets. As milling approaches uncertain boundaries, the robot actively probes the remaining structure and uses relative stiffness changes to estimate boundary status and structural detachability. A state-adaptive controller governs transitions between active perception and spatially selective incremental refinement, repeating this cycle until the termination criterion is satisfied. Hierarchical experiments on biological surrogates and in vivo mouse cranial window creation demonstrate accurate anatomical prior transfer, reliable boundary adaptation, and autonomous precision milling of biological structures.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yitian Pang, Yifan Li, Xiaowei Yue, Li Zheng
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: GOPR-CAD introduces a novel Text-to-CAD pipeline using Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning to enhance structural fidelity in CAD model generation, achieving high structural yields.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: RoadState: A Domain-Prior-Enhanced Vision-Language System for Industrial-Grade Lane-Level Map Updating
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Deguo Xia, Zihan Li, Jiaqi Wang, Dong Xie, Xiyan Liu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: RoadState is a vision-language system that enhances lane-level map updating through autoregressive state estimation and domain-prior reasoning, achieving high accuracy and cost reduction in real-world applications.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Lane-level map updating requires temporally consistent, physically valid, and auditable road-scene semantics despite occlusions, ambiguous lane markings, temporary obstacles, and viewpoint changes. We present RoadState, a production-deployed vision-language system that transforms sequential road-scene observations into structured lane-level semantics for Baidu Maps' map-updating pipeline. Its core model, RoadState-VLM, formulates road-scene understanding as autoregressive state estimation, predicting the current structured road state from the previous observation and symbolic state together with the current observation. We introduce Geometric Chain-of-Thought (Geo-CoT), which uses a directed acyclic graph of semantic dependencies as a domain prior to improve semantic consistency and reasoning fidelity across interdependent road-state dimensions. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset show that RoadState-VLM achieves 94.33% mean accuracy across six road-state dimensions, outperforming the strongest fine-tuned VLM baseline. Ablation studies further demonstrate the complementary effectiveness of Geo-CoT and temporal transition context. A cascaded routing pipeline directs routine cases to lightweight models while reserving complex cases for RoadState-VLM. Since its deployment in March 2025, RoadState has supported lane-level map updating across more than 360 cities and reduced overall production costs by 30%. Together with human-in-the-loop auditing, the system maintains robust performance under stress-test conditions. These results demonstrate how domain-prior-enhanced reasoning, structured state interfaces, selective routing, and human quality control can bridge the gap between VLM-based road-scene understanding and large-scale lane-level map updating.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Beyond Action Residuals: Real-World Robot Policy Steering via Bottleneck Latent Reinforcement Learning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Dongjie Yu, Kun Lei, Zhennan Jiang, Jia Pan, Huazhe Xu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), which enhances pretrained robot policies through a compact bottleneck latent interface, improving adaptation and performance in real-world tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Pretrained imitation policies have become a strong foundation for robot manipulation, but online adaptation can further improve policy performance within their pretrained behavioral support. A central question is therefore how reinforcement learning (RL) should adapt policies after offline pretraining. Existing lightweight methods commonly apply residual corrections directly in action space. We investigate how the steering interface affects online RL. In this work, we propose Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), an approach that steers pretrained policies through a compact bottleneck latent rather than through policy weights or output actions.
