Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: Embodied First Exam
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Kangrui Wang, Qineng Wang, Changhe Chen, Pingyue Zhang, Chi Gui
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: The Embodied First Exam introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework for coding agents controlling diverse robots, assessing their performance across 1,156 tasks and various settings.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. We hope it serves as a first exam for coding agents before they enter the physical world, with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites that go beyond pick-and-place to spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering. Each task can be run in up to three evaluation settings. The Standard Setting mimics the real world: the agent receives only sensor observations and, by default, cannot reset the environment. Its Realtime variant keeps the environment running while the agent reasons. The Privileged Setting gives the agent access to the full simulator state and unlimited resets, allowing it to search for an oracle solution for training purposes. Success rates in this setting serve as an approximate upper bound. On the 456 core tasks, the strongest of eight agents, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, achieves a success rate of 34% in the Standard Setting, leaving much room for improvement. To see where agents fail, we label the stage at which failed attempts go wrong and compare failures across agents, settings, and stage categories.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: UniLatent: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Latent Observation Alignment
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Yufei Ding, Yi Du, Weiduo Yuan, Hao Jiang, Dylan Goetting
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: UniLatent is a framework that enables effective cross-embodiment transfer of robotic skills by aligning latent observations, achieving high success rates without pixel-level translation.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Robot datasets are costly to collect and are usually tied to a specific embodiment, making it difficult to reuse demonstrations across robots with different geometry, appearance, and kinematics. We introduce UniLatent, a cross-embodiment transfer framework that reduces the embodiment-induced observation gap in a shared latent space. UniLatent renders paired source-target robot observations in simulation and aligns a source visual encoder to a frozen target encoder. A policy trained on encoded source demonstrations can then run directly on target observations, with no pixel-level image translation. Across three simulation tasks and two target robot arms, UniLatent reaches up to 93% zero-shot success, exceeding the strongest pixel-translation baseline by over 30 points on average. In real-world xArm-to-Franka transfer, fine-tuning with only 10 target demonstrations per task yields 27/30 successful rollouts. Code, videos and data are available at https://selina2023.github.io/unilatent/.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: Mental Imagery That Matters: Curing Latent Collapse in Multimodal Reasoning
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Mi Luo, Rohan Dugad, Zihui Xue, Alex Dimakis, Kristen Grauman
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: The paper identifies "Mental Simulation Collapse" in multimodal reasoning models, revealing that visual latents often lack impact on outcomes, and proposes AnchorSim to enhance their significance.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Mental simulation, the ability to reason by constructing and updating internal visual states, is central to flexible human cognition, but remains elusive in current multimodal large language models. Latent multimodal reasoning offers a promising route toward this capability by interleaving text with continuous visual latent blocks, allowing models to maintain internal visual workspaces without decoding them into pixels. In this paper, we ask whether these latent visual states actually matter. Through a direct perturbation analysis across representative latent-reasoning MLLMs, we find that they often do not: dropping, replacing, or shuffling generated visual latents has only minor effects on the model's own final-answer probability, while equivalent perturbations to the linguistic reasoning trace are substantially more damaging. We call this failure mode Mental Simulation Collapse (MSC): the model appears to perform interleaved visual reasoning, but routes most answer-relevant computation through text. We further diagnose that MSC follows naturally from existing training objectives: visual alignment can make generated latents resemble helper-image embeddings, but it does not require the decoder to rely on them; subsequent text-only supervision further leaves the semantic role of the latent pathway unidentifiable. To address this, we introduce AnchorSim (Anchored Mental Simulation), a contrastive distillation framework that trains models to make their generated visual latents consequential. Across multiple visual reasoning benchmarks, AnchorSim improves performance, while diagnostic re-evaluation shows that visual perturbations now meaningfully affect predictions. Our results expose a fundamental failure mode of latent multimodal reasoning and demonstrate that mental simulation must be anchored to model behavior in order to matter.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: A Unified Inertial Encoder for Human and Humanoid Motion
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Yutian Chen, Shibo Zhao, Rocky Duan, Karen Liu, Carmelo Sferrazza
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: The paper presents a unified inertial encoder that enables effective transfer of human motion knowledge to humanoid robots, achieving superior velocity estimation and motion understanding without prior fine-tuning.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Learning humanoid state estimation and language-grounded motion understanding from robot recordings ties training coverage to the robot's motion repertoire. Human motion datasets offer broader coverage, yet transferring this knowledge requires overcoming differences in body geometry, sensing, and physical disturbances. To enable this transfer, we propose a unified inertial encoder whose shared inertial interface uses kinematic IMU synthesis to represent human and humanoid motion at corresponding body sites. Within this common input space, joint training on human and kinematically retargeted humanoid motion combines velocity estimation and motion--text alignment with continuous-time encoding and sensor and motion randomization. The resulting model transfers zero-shot to a physical Unitree G1 without physics simulation, real-robot training trajectories, or fine-tuning, achieving the lowest velocity error among evaluated methods across five datasets, including 0.099m/s on real G1. Its motion-description retrieval also extends to retargeted G1 motion categories observed only in human training, demonstrating how human motion knowledge can support the generalization of humanoid inertial odometry and language-grounded motion understanding.

南方科技大学.title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation
南方科技大学.authors_text: Jinghe Wang, Xinrui Cao, Duo Wu, Chenghao Gu, Yong Zhong
南方科技大学.summary: GeoMind is a new benchmark for evaluating spatial understanding in robotic manipulation, focusing on spatial reasoning and memory through diverse, automated tabletop tasks.
南方科技大学.debug_abstract: Robotic manipulation has advanced rapidly in mapping visual observations and language instructions to actions. However, reliable manipulation in open-world environments requires robust spatial understanding: the ability to identify targets in complex layouts (spatial reasoning) and adapt to scenes that continuously evolve through interaction (spatial memory). Yet existing embodied benchmarks fall short in evaluating spatial understanding: they often introduce strong visual cues that bypass spatial reasoning, and focus on static scenes that offer little insight into an agent's capacity for spatial memory. To address this gap, we introduce GeoMind, a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation. GeoMind comprises 54 evaluated task variants organized around spatial reasoning and spatial memory. It also incorporates a scalable pipeline that automates the generation and annotation of task instances with verified targets and executable interactions. Extensive evaluations across diverse embodied agents reveal their consistent weaknesses in spatial understanding. Our findings highlight that these agents struggle to track identities after spatial changes and convert relational or geometric constraints into executable actions. We release the GeoMind benchmark at https://github.com/Notfound-JH/GEOMIND-benchmark.git.

南方科技大学.title: Embodied AI for Scientific Discovery: From Physical Action to Scientific Evidence
南方科技大学.authors_text: Wenhao Xu, Changwei Wang, Shunpeng Chen, Yukun Song, Sifan Zhou
南方科技大学.summary: This review explores embodied AI's role in scientific discovery, integrating robot learning and experiment selection through a structured framework of operational, epistemic, and evidential closures.
南方科技大学.debug_abstract: Scientific experiments are increasingly selected, executed and interpreted by learned systems that act through physical interfaces. Robot learning builds physical competence, whereas AI for science chooses which experiment to run, each reporting different endpoints. This review treats their interface as one problem, embodied AI for science, where the experiment itself is partially observed: specimen state, apparatus state and measurement processes are latent, actions are costly and irreversible, and missingness depends on execution and outcome. We organize the literature by three closures operating at distinct levels: operational closure (the experiment realized is the one intended), epistemic closure (the result updates beliefs or selects subsequent experiments) and evidential closure (the record supports a claim). We analyze workflows through a record-linked evidence cycle - Record, Diagnose, Calibrate, Confirm - as analytic functions with feedback. A taxonomy crosses these closures with six delegated decisions and five embodiment classes. Our formulation separates commanded, realized and observed conditions and models diagnosis with explicit resource, risk and sample-change costs. We compare experiment-selection methods by terminal decision, review perception, protocol compilation, visuomotor policies, world models, recovery and transfer by evidence emission requirements, and compare chemistry, materials, biology, microscopy and field workflows by what their records establish. An appendix provides an evidence map of 28 workflows (26 physical, two software-boundary), characterizing validation pathways and claim confirmation requirements. We propose evaluation that separates actions, valid experiments, campaigns and confirmed claims, framing open challenges as controlled comparisons with measurable failure conditions.

南方科技大学.title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design
南方科技大学.summary: This paper introduces a mobility information capacity framework for multi-robot systems, optimizing maneuver design under safety constraints to enhance observable motion variability.
南方科技大学.debug_abstract: Multiple robots operating in shared workspaces must adjust their speed, direction, and trajectories to coordinate with one another and respond to changing tasks and disturbances. The available maneuver freedom depends on the dynamics, uncertainty, and safety margins, even for a fixed fleet size and workspace. However, robot count, workspace occupancy, and task throughput do not quantify how much the fleet can vary its motion or how reliably these variations can be observed. We develop a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that jointly characterizes these two aspects. Mobility information is defined as the mutual information between a joint maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation, and MIC maximizes this quantity under maneuver-resource constraints. For a linear Gaussian maneuver-to-observation model with feedback dynamics, we characterize the finite-horizon information benchmark and derive its stationary long-horizon spectral limit, accounting for heterogeneous mobility gains, colored uncertainty, and temporally coupled maneuver costs. We further map workspace-boundary, inter-robot separation, and actuator chance constraints into coupled maneuver-covariance restrictions and derive conditions under which covariance optimization reduces to resource allocation across mobility modes. Finite joint maneuver codebooks are then constructed through individual risk screening and noise-whitened trajectory separation, with bounds linking sequence recovery error and achieved information to the capacity benchmarks. An aerial-robot simulation study evaluates spectral convergence, safety-aware allocation, finite-codebook identification, and fleet-size scaling. The resulting framework complements occupancy and task-throughput measures by quantifying the maximum observable maneuver freedom supported by a mobility system.

ReThinkLab.title: SurgTAP-3D: A Large-Scale Cross-Surgery Video Dataset with Contact-Aware 3D Motion Tracking
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Jiaxin Guo, Wenzhen Dong, Taoyu Wu, Haomin Kuang, Mengya Xu
ReThinkLab.summary: SurgTAP-3D is a comprehensive dataset for 3D motion tracking in minimally invasive surgery, addressing tool-tissue interactions and enhancing autonomous surgical system development.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Understanding 3D scene dynamics in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is a fundamental step toward physically intelligent and autonomous surgical systems. However, existing public datasets offer limited scalability and diversity in real-world clinical scenarios. Moreover, annotations typically focus on either tissue or instruments alone, overlooking tool-tissue interactions. This gap limits applications such as augmented reality guidance and autonomous surgery driven by vision-language-action (VLA) models or world models, which demand large-scale, high-quality 3D supervision. In this work, we construct SurgTAP-3D, a large-scale in-vivo pseudo-3D surgical motion tracking dataset and benchmark, comprising 520K frames, 4,549 action clips, and 1.4M 2D/3D point trajectories from diverse robotic and manual procedures under unified action categories. To make annotation scalable, we design a unified framework for surgical 3D point tracking that converts uncalibrated monocular surgical videos into structured 4D annotations through contact-region prompting, active-tool segmentation, dynamic bundle adjustment, and global 4D refinement. This pipeline adapts foundation priors to surgical videos and produces temporally consistent trajectories, pseudo-scale geometry, camera poses, and instrument masks. The dataset captures realistic challenges inherent to surgical environments, including occlusions, smoke, bleeding, and rapid instrument motion. We establish a comprehensive benchmark on SurgPose, SurgT, and STIR, covering both instrument and tissue tracking. We demonstrate instrument displacement estimation, deformable surface reconstruction, and foundation-model fine-tuning. Extensive experiments and analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset and annotation framework for 3D surgical point tracking, reconstruction, and surgical action understanding. Homepage: https://wrld.github.io/surgtap-3d/

ReThinkLab.title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Ziyang Zeng, Tingyang Chen, Jia Deng, Qiyao Wang, Shuo Tang
ReThinkLab.summary: WorkFactory is a framework that transforms professional intents into executable tasks, enhancing agent training through improved task environment quality and scalable task construction.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Scaling supervised fine-tuning for working agents requires not only broad coverage of professional tasks, but also expert demonstrations that faithfully carry out professional workflows to completion. However, missing or inconsistent task information can disrupt expert demonstrations, weakening the resulting supervision. We introduce WorkFactory, a scalable task-construction framework that turns professional intents into executable task environments through hybrid intent sourcing, semantic workflow planning, and execution-based repair. Starting from these intents, WorkFactory constructs a Semantic Workflow Graph that explicitly represents information requirements, dependencies, and locations within the task environment. The graph guides the instantiation of task environments, while an adversarial execution-refinement loop exposes missing or inconsistent information and steers targeted repairs that preserve the original intent. Using WorkFactory, we construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and train the WorkPilot family at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales on the resulting teacher trajectories. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B rising from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. Scaling experiments with up to 110k tasks further show that larger models benefit more from additional task data but exhibit diminishing returns at smaller data scales, while WorkPilot's long-horizon execution evolves from verbose trajectories toward more efficient task completion. Controlled component studies quantify the negative effects of task-environment defects on downstream performance and show how semantic workflow planning and execution-based repair yield downstream gains through improved task-environment quality. The subset of data are available at https://github.com/IQuestLab/WorkFactory.

ReThinkLab.title: AetheRock: An Arm-Worn Robot Teaching System for Force-Guided Vision-Tactile Learning
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Hong Li, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Yankang Dong, Chenyuan Liu
ReThinkLab.summary: AetheRock is an arm-worn robot system that enhances force-guided vision-tactile learning through improved sensor integration and a novel multimodal representation framework.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Force and tactile sensing are essential for contact-rich manipulation, but their integration into handheld or wearable devices is constrained by cost, size, and mechanical compatibility. Tactile signals are also sensitive to manufacturing variations and wear during use, posing further challenges to policy learning. To address these hardware and learning challenges, we introduce AetheRock, an arm-worn device for collecting gripper-force, visual, and tactile data. AetheRock incorporates GelSlim-Mini, our improved version of GelSlim 4.0 designed for low-cost, easy manufacturing, at the gripper fingertip, together with a resistive pressure sensor at the human finger contact area. To learn robust representations from the collected data, we propose ForceVT, a framework that aligns multimodal representations and uses force and vision to guide tactile learning, mitigating the effects of manufacturing variations and sensor degradation. Real-world experiments demonstrate efficient data collection with AetheRock. ForceVT improves average performance by 13% over the vision-tactile baseline and maintains an average task progress of 55.0% under reduced tactile fidelity, compared with 58.0% at full fidelity. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/aetherock.

ReThinkLab.title: Beyond Action Residuals: Real-World Robot Policy Steering via Bottleneck Latent Reinforcement Learning
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Dongjie Yu, Kun Lei, Zhennan Jiang, Jia Pan, Huazhe Xu
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper presents Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), which enhances pretrained robot policies through a compact bottleneck latent interface, improving adaptation and performance in real-world tasks.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Pretrained imitation policies have become a strong foundation for robot manipulation, but online adaptation can further improve policy performance within their pretrained behavioral support. A central question is therefore how reinforcement learning (RL) should adapt policies after offline pretraining. Existing lightweight methods commonly apply residual corrections directly in action space. We investigate how the steering interface affects online RL. In this work, we propose Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), an approach that steers pretrained policies through a compact bottleneck latent rather than through policy weights or output actions. Building on an offline-learned bottleneck policy interface introduced by previous work, ZPRL turns this representation into an online RL control space through reward-driven residual perturbations while freezing the pretrained policy. We instantiate ZPRL on flow-matching policies and evaluate it on eight simulation tasks and four real-world tasks. Across diverse manipulation settings, ZPRL improves sample efficiency with competitive or better final performance. In the real world, ZPRL improves the average success rate on four tasks by 33.7 percentage points over imitation base policies. Our qualitative and quantitative results also indicate that ZPRL combines task success with smooth actions without explicit temporal filtering or smoothness regularization. These results suggest that a compact, task-aligned bottleneck latent provides an effective interface for online RL adaptation. Videos and code can be found at https://manutdmoon.github.io/ZPRL/.

ReThinkLab.title: DAPointRWKV: Domain Adaptive Vision RWKV for Point Cloud Completion
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Yinghui Li, Qianyu Zhou, Hao Yang, Richard Dazeley, Ye Zhu
ReThinkLab.summary: DAPointRWKV introduces a novel RWKV-based framework for domain adaptive point cloud completion, addressing geometric discrepancies and enhancing performance through geometry-aware learning and structural regularization.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Domain adaptive point cloud completion (DA PCC) aims to bridge the geometric discrepancy between labeled source domains and unlabeled target domains for accurate 3D shape completion. Existing methods based on CNNs, Transformers, and Mamba-like sequence models still face challenges from limited receptive fields, high computational complexity, insufficient geometric bias, and serialization sensitivity. Recently, Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) provides a linear-complexity alternative for long-range sequence modeling. However, adapting RWKV to DA PCC remains challenging due to the lack of explicit geometric priors, the mismatch between recurrent modeling and coarse-to-fine generation, and unstable target-domain adaptation. To address these challenges, we propose DAPointRWKV, a novel RWKV-based framework for DA PCC. DAPointRWKV consists of three components: Geometry-Aware RWKV (GA-RWKV) Backbone, RWKV-Oriented Progressive Decoder (RWKV-PD), and Dual Structural Regularization (DSR). Specifically, GA-RWKV introduces geometry-aware recurrent representation learning, RWKV-PD bridges RWKV token representations with coarse-to-fine reconstruction through local token-guided refinement, and DSR stabilizes target-domain transfer through visible-structure anchoring and complete-shape hypothesis stabilization. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that DAPointRWKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

ReThinkLab.title: HuMI: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Humanoid-Free Demonstrations
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Ruiqian Nai, Boyuan Zheng, Junming Zhao, Haodong Zhu, Sicong Dai
ReThinkLab.summary: HuMI is a portable framework that enhances humanoid whole-body manipulation by efficiently learning from humanoid-free demonstrations, achieving significant improvements in data collection and task success rates.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Current approaches for humanoid whole-body manipulation, primarily relying on teleoperation or visual sim-to-real reinforcement learning, are hindered by hardware logistics and complex reward engineering. Consequently, demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments. In this paper, we present the Humanoid Manipulation Interface (HuMI), a portable and efficient framework for learning diverse whole-body manipulation tasks across various environments. HuMI enables humanoid-free data collection by capturing rich whole-body motion using portable hardware. This data drives a hierarchical learning pipeline that translates human motions into dexterous and feasible humanoid skills. Extensive experiments across five whole-body tasks--including kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual manipulation--demonstrate that HuMI achieves a 3x increase in data collection efficiency compared to teleoperation and attains a 70% success rate in unseen environments.

ReThinkLab.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang, Yinghao Yang, Wendi Chen
ReThinkLab.summary: The SWAM paper presents a scalable world action model that enhances language-video-action alignment through extensive data curation and optimized training strategies, achieving significant performance improvements in real-world tasks.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

ReThinkLab.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Zheng Wang, Zhengwei Gong, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang
ReThinkLab.summary: MotionCore is a latent neural simulator that enhances video generation by integrating learned rigid-body dynamics with visual modeling for improved physical consistency and trajectory fidelity.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable partial differential equation solver and focuses on rigid-body motion. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. To preserve this trajectory through the interface, MotionCore combines a diffusion-matching objective with a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical-consistency benchmarks and on paired data with known trajectories. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. A controlled ablation protocol compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.

ReThinkLab.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Shuyuan Hu, Deng-Ke Wu, Yifan Jin, Qianhang Luo, Mingchen Ju
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper introduces Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR) to enhance bimanual imitation learning by reducing spurious cross-arm coupling while preserving task-relevant constraints.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%. With $π_{0.5}$ on an Independent task, a 4 s pause transfers 2.56 s of delay to the opposite arm under the Concurrent schedule distribution, but only 0.25 s with CTR. On real robots, CTR violates task constraints in only 0--4% of trials, versus 36--98% for narrow-schedule baselines. Code will be released at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/CTR.

ReThinkLab.title: Towards Rotation-Only Imaging Geometry: Multi-View Pose Estimation
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Xinrui Li, Qi Cai, Yuanxin Wu
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper presents GRAM and MORE, novel methods for estimating global rotations and translations in multi-view pose estimation by minimizing rotation-only algebraic residuals, enhancing accuracy and efficiency.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Global structure-from-motion (SfM) commonly refines relative poses on individual image pairs and then estimates global rotations by rotation averaging. Pairwise refinement does not explicitly combine feature-level constraints with multi-view consistency during rotation initialization. We introduce Global Rotations from Aggregated Matches (GRAM), which estimates global rotations directly from initial relative rotations and inlier matches by minimizing edge-wise rotation-only algebraic residuals. GRAM replaces two-view relative-pose optimization and rotation averaging with a single stage. We further extend rotation- only imaging geometry to multiple views and develop Multi-view Optimization with Rotation-only Reprojection Error (MORE) for nonlinear global rotation refinement. Analytical Rotation-guided Translation (ART) derives locally scaled triplet translations from Linear Global Translation (LiGT) constraints and recovers global translations using weighted least squares. Synthetic and real-world experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and efficiency of the proposed methods.

ReThinkLab.title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Yude Zou, Yifei Yao, Yiwei Hao, Hanqing Wang, Xing Gao
ReThinkLab.summary: InfCoiL introduces a closed-loop framework for human-object interaction that integrates a morphology-aware planner and a multi-morphology controller, enhancing performance through coordinated learning and reinforcement.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Text- and goal-conditioned human-object interaction (HOI) provides an intuitive interface for specifying high-level intents in physics-based character animation. Mapping such intents to physically plausible, contact-rich behaviors naturally calls for a generative planner and a physics-based controller, yet existing planner-controller systems either execute plans open-loop or close the loop while keeping the planner fixed, so execution feedback never reshapes what is planned. We present InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based HOI from coordinated planner-controller learning. InfCoiL couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller through a shared morphology interface in an autoregressive plan-and-execute loop, and alternately fine-tunes both components with reinforcement learning from the same physical rollouts. To optimize the flow-matching planner online, we introduce Semantic Flow Policy Optimization (SFPO), which stochasticizes selected denoising transitions with channel-wise semantic covariance over heterogeneous HOI features and assigns group-relative, sequence-level rewards from complete closed-loop executions. On held-out OMOMO sequences, InfCoiL outperforms open-loop hierarchical baselines in goal-reaching task success and physical tracking accuracy. Project page: https://infcoil.github.io/

ReThinkLab.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Xing Gao, Guanbo Jiao, Yukai Wang
ReThinkLab.summary: The paper introduces SimplEvo, a memory evolution framework for embodied agents that enhances performance without weight updates, achieving significant success rate improvements in task execution.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

ReThinkLab.title: Efficient VLA Inference via Retrieval-Based Speculation and Hardware Acceleration
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Zhengyang Cheng, He Zhu, Zeyu Guo, Zihan Liu, Anbang Wu
ReThinkLab.summary: Zora is a hardware-software framework that accelerates vision-language-action inference by utilizing a lightweight retrieval model and optimizing action verification, achieving significant speedups on edge platforms.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to understand and execute complex instructions, but their autoregressive (AR) action generation introduces significant latency on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Speculative decoding can accelerate AR-based inference by parallelizing action generation and verification; however, existing approaches rely on costly draft models, which are inefficient on edge platforms. In this paper, we propose Zora, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference. Specifically, Zora introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models. We further reduce batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism. To address the retrieval overhead introduced by RAG-based drafting, we co-design dedicated hardware support, Zora core, to address the memory irregularity in RAG-based drafting. We evaluate Zora on four VLA models with the LIBERO benchmark. Zora retains comparable accuracy while achieving up to 3.4$\times$ speedup with software-only optimization and up to 7.6$\times$ speedup with hardware support over GPUs.

ReThinkLab.title: WARP-JEPA: World-Model-in-the-Loop Amortized Rollout Planning for Frozen Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Junjie Li, Zhaojiacheng Zhou, Kaixiang Wang, Zihan Wang, QingSong Zhao
ReThinkLab.summary: WARP-JEPA enhances long-horizon visual control by replacing costly gradient descent with efficient learned trajectory proposers, achieving significant speed and success improvements in planning.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (H-JEPA) enable long-horizon visual control but rely on costly test-time gradient descent for planning. Our analysis reveals that iterative optimization consumes up to 97.7% of episode runtime and that low predicted rollout costs do not necessarily translate into successful control. We further identify a planning-horizon asymmetry between long-horizon top-level composition and short two-step subordinate planning. To address these challenges, we propose WARP-JEPA, a hierarchical amortized planning framework that replaces online gradient optimization with learned multi-candidate trajectory proposers while keeping the world models frozen. WARP-JEPA combines a lightweight world-model-in-the-loop causal Transformer at the top level with parallel residual MLPs at subordinate levels. The proposers are trained using model-based rollout costs and best-of-K behavior cloning, enabling efficient candidate selection without test-time gradient optimization. Across 30 frozen H-JEPA models on four benchmarks, WARP-JEPA achieves 9.6-18.8x faster episode inference on long-horizon tasks (2.9-3.0x on Cube) and improves task success by up to 33.3 percentage points. These results demonstrate that amortized planning can substantially improve both inference efficiency and control performance without retraining the world models. Code is available at https://github.com/hideinsewer/WARP-JEPA.

ReThinkLab.title: Tac-DINO: Learning Tactile Features with Patch Alignment
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Hong Li, Yankang Dong, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Jiamin Qiu
ReThinkLab.summary: Tac-DINO introduces a novel dataset and learning framework that enhances tactile perception in robotic manipulation through improved patch-level alignment and geometric supervision.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Multisensory perception is essential for robotic manipulation, with tactile sensing providing critical information for fine-grained, contact-rich interactions. Although prior work integrates tactile and spatial signals to improve perception, vision-tactile learning commonly relies on object-level alignment. Addressing this limitation requires systematically aligned 3D vision-tactile data. We develop a data collection system and introduce Touch3D, a dataset comprising 505 real-world objects and 20,025 tactile contacts. Building on this dataset, we establish the Contact-Centric Multimodal Tactile Representation Benchmark (CoMT-Bench), which expands evaluation from object-level retrieval and tactile properties to include patch-level contact evaluation. We further propose Geometry-Relation Distilled Tactile-Centric Cross-Modal Learning (GeoTAC), which explores tactile learning across all multisensory data. In experiments on the Touch3D test set, patch-level alignment improves the average score by 5.32 over object-level alignment, with GeoTAC's geometric supervision improving it by a further 4.48. In robotic manipulation, GeoTAC improves TP by 19.14 and 11.34 over DINOv2 (Vision-only) and DINOv2 (Vision-Tactile), respectively. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/tacdino.

ReThinkLab.title: LSRP*: Scalable and Anytime Planning for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Asynchronous Actions
ReThinkLab.authors_text: Dachuan Liu, Shuai Zhou, Shizhe Zhao, Zhongqiang Ren
ReThinkLab.summary: LSRP* is an improved anytime planner for Multi-Agent Path Finding that enhances solution quality and scalability, accommodating more agents and reducing costs compared to LSRP.
ReThinkLab.debug_abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their respective starting locations to their respective goal locations while minimizing path costs. Although many MAPF algorithms were developed, most of them rely on a common assumption on synchronized actions, where the actions of all agents start at the same time and always take a time unit. This assumption may limit the use of MAPF planners in practice. To get rid of this assumption, recently, an algorithm called Loosely Synchronized Rule-based Planning (LSRP) was proposed, which can find sub-optimal solutions for many agents. However, LSRP often finds poor quality solutions due to its unbounded sub-optimality. This paper develops a new anytime planner called LSRP* that can keep improving solution quality after the initial solution is obtained until the runtime budget depletes. We analyze the properties of LSRP* and test it against several baselines with up to 1000 agents on various maps. LSRP* can handle up to 25% more agents than LSRP and can reduce up to 40% of the solution cost found by LSRP.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Ziyang Zeng, Tingyang Chen, Jia Deng, Qiyao Wang, Shuo Tang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: WorkFactory is a framework that transforms professional intents into executable tasks, enhancing agent training through improved task environment quality and scalable task construction.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Scaling supervised fine-tuning for working agents requires not only broad coverage of professional tasks, but also expert demonstrations that faithfully carry out professional workflows to completion. However, missing or inconsistent task information can disrupt expert demonstrations, weakening the resulting supervision. We introduce WorkFactory, a scalable task-construction framework that turns professional intents into executable task environments through hybrid intent sourcing, semantic workflow planning, and execution-based repair. Starting from these intents, WorkFactory constructs a Semantic Workflow Graph that explicitly represents information requirements, dependencies, and locations within the task environment. The graph guides the instantiation of task environments, while an adversarial execution-refinement loop exposes missing or inconsistent information and steers targeted repairs that preserve the original intent. Using WorkFactory, we construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and train the WorkPilot family at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales on the resulting teacher trajectories. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B rising from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. Scaling experiments with up to 110k tasks further show that larger models benefit more from additional task data but exhibit diminishing returns at smaller data scales, while WorkPilot's long-horizon execution evolves from verbose trajectories toward more efficient task completion. Controlled component studies quantify the negative effects of task-environment defects on downstream performance and show how semantic workflow planning and execution-based repair yield downstream gains through improved task-environment quality. The subset of data are available at https://github.com/IQuestLab/WorkFactory.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: AetheRock: An Arm-Worn Robot Teaching System for Force-Guided Vision-Tactile Learning
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Hong Li, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Yankang Dong, Chenyuan Liu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: AetheRock is an arm-worn robot system that enhances force-guided vision-tactile learning through improved sensor integration and a novel multimodal representation framework.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Force and tactile sensing are essential for contact-rich manipulation, but their integration into handheld or wearable devices is constrained by cost, size, and mechanical compatibility. Tactile signals are also sensitive to manufacturing variations and wear during use, posing further challenges to policy learning. To address these hardware and learning challenges, we introduce AetheRock, an arm-worn device for collecting gripper-force, visual, and tactile data. AetheRock incorporates GelSlim-Mini, our improved version of GelSlim 4.0 designed for low-cost, easy manufacturing, at the gripper fingertip, together with a resistive pressure sensor at the human finger contact area. To learn robust representations from the collected data, we propose ForceVT, a framework that aligns multimodal representations and uses force and vision to guide tactile learning, mitigating the effects of manufacturing variations and sensor degradation. Real-world experiments demonstrate efficient data collection with AetheRock. ForceVT improves average performance by 13% over the vision-tactile baseline and maintains an average task progress of 55.0% under reduced tactile fidelity, compared with 58.0% at full fidelity. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/aetherock.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Beyond Action Residuals: Real-World Robot Policy Steering via Bottleneck Latent Reinforcement Learning
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Dongjie Yu, Kun Lei, Zhennan Jiang, Jia Pan, Huazhe Xu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), which enhances pretrained robot policies through a compact bottleneck latent interface, improving adaptation and performance in real-world tasks.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Pretrained imitation policies have become a strong foundation for robot manipulation, but online adaptation can further improve policy performance within their pretrained behavioral support. A central question is therefore how reinforcement learning (RL) should adapt policies after offline pretraining. Existing lightweight methods commonly apply residual corrections directly in action space. We investigate how the steering interface affects online RL. In this work, we propose Z-Perturbation Reinforcement Learning (ZPRL), an approach that steers pretrained policies through a compact bottleneck latent rather than through policy weights or output actions. Building on an offline-learned bottleneck policy interface introduced by previous work, ZPRL turns this representation into an online RL control space through reward-driven residual perturbations while freezing the pretrained policy. We instantiate ZPRL on flow-matching policies and evaluate it on eight simulation tasks and four real-world tasks. Across diverse manipulation settings, ZPRL improves sample efficiency with competitive or better final performance. In the real world, ZPRL improves the average success rate on four tasks by 33.7 percentage points over imitation base policies. Our qualitative and quantitative results also indicate that ZPRL combines task success with smooth actions without explicit temporal filtering or smoothness regularization. These results suggest that a compact, task-aligned bottleneck latent provides an effective interface for online RL adaptation. Videos and code can be found at https://manutdmoon.github.io/ZPRL/.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: DAPointRWKV: Domain Adaptive Vision RWKV for Point Cloud Completion
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yinghui Li, Qianyu Zhou, Hao Yang, Richard Dazeley, Ye Zhu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: DAPointRWKV introduces a novel RWKV-based framework for domain adaptive point cloud completion, addressing geometric discrepancies and enhancing performance through geometry-aware learning and structural regularization.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Domain adaptive point cloud completion (DA PCC) aims to bridge the geometric discrepancy between labeled source domains and unlabeled target domains for accurate 3D shape completion. Existing methods based on CNNs, Transformers, and Mamba-like sequence models still face challenges from limited receptive fields, high computational complexity, insufficient geometric bias, and serialization sensitivity. Recently, Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) provides a linear-complexity alternative for long-range sequence modeling. However, adapting RWKV to DA PCC remains challenging due to the lack of explicit geometric priors, the mismatch between recurrent modeling and coarse-to-fine generation, and unstable target-domain adaptation. To address these challenges, we propose DAPointRWKV, a novel RWKV-based framework for DA PCC. DAPointRWKV consists of three components: Geometry-Aware RWKV (GA-RWKV) Backbone, RWKV-Oriented Progressive Decoder (RWKV-PD), and Dual Structural Regularization (DSR). Specifically, GA-RWKV introduces geometry-aware recurrent representation learning, RWKV-PD bridges RWKV token representations with coarse-to-fine reconstruction through local token-guided refinement, and DSR stabilizes target-domain transfer through visible-structure anchoring and complete-shape hypothesis stabilization. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that DAPointRWKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: HuMI: Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation from Humanoid-Free Demonstrations
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Ruiqian Nai, Boyuan Zheng, Junming Zhao, Haodong Zhu, Sicong Dai
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: HuMI is a portable framework that enhances humanoid whole-body manipulation by efficiently learning from humanoid-free demonstrations, achieving significant improvements in data collection and task success rates.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Current approaches for humanoid whole-body manipulation, primarily relying on teleoperation or visual sim-to-real reinforcement learning, are hindered by hardware logistics and complex reward engineering. Consequently, demonstrated autonomous skills remain limited and are typically restricted to controlled environments. In this paper, we present the Humanoid Manipulation Interface (HuMI), a portable and efficient framework for learning diverse whole-body manipulation tasks across various environments. HuMI enables humanoid-free data collection by capturing rich whole-body motion using portable hardware. This data drives a hierarchical learning pipeline that translates human motions into dexterous and feasible humanoid skills. Extensive experiments across five whole-body tasks--including kneeling, squatting, tossing, walking, and bimanual manipulation--demonstrate that HuMI achieves a 3x increase in data collection efficiency compared to teleoperation and attains a 70% success rate in unseen environments.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang, Yinghao Yang, Wendi Chen
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The SWAM paper presents a scalable world action model that enhances language-video-action alignment through extensive data curation and optimized training strategies, achieving significant performance improvements in real-world tasks.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zheng Wang, Zhengwei Gong, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: MotionCore is a latent neural simulator that enhances video generation by integrating learned rigid-body dynamics with visual modeling for improved physical consistency and trajectory fidelity.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable partial differential equation solver and focuses on rigid-body motion. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. To preserve this trajectory through the interface, MotionCore combines a diffusion-matching objective with a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical-consistency benchmarks and on paired data with known trajectories. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. A controlled ablation protocol compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Shuyuan Hu, Deng-Ke Wu, Yifan Jin, Qianhang Luo, Mingchen Ju
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper introduces Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR) to enhance bimanual imitation learning by reducing spurious cross-arm coupling while preserving task-relevant constraints.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%. With $π_{0.5}$ on an Independent task, a 4 s pause transfers 2.56 s of delay to the opposite arm under the Concurrent schedule distribution, but only 0.25 s with CTR. On real robots, CTR violates task constraints in only 0--4% of trials, versus 36--98% for narrow-schedule baselines. Code will be released at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/CTR.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Towards Rotation-Only Imaging Geometry: Multi-View Pose Estimation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Xinrui Li, Qi Cai, Yuanxin Wu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents GRAM and MORE, novel methods for estimating global rotations and translations in multi-view pose estimation by minimizing rotation-only algebraic residuals, enhancing accuracy and efficiency.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Global structure-from-motion (SfM) commonly refines relative poses on individual image pairs and then estimates global rotations by rotation averaging. Pairwise refinement does not explicitly combine feature-level constraints with multi-view consistency during rotation initialization. We introduce Global Rotations from Aggregated Matches (GRAM), which estimates global rotations directly from initial relative rotations and inlier matches by minimizing edge-wise rotation-only algebraic residuals. GRAM replaces two-view relative-pose optimization and rotation averaging with a single stage. We further extend rotation- only imaging geometry to multiple views and develop Multi-view Optimization with Rotation-only Reprojection Error (MORE) for nonlinear global rotation refinement. Analytical Rotation-guided Translation (ART) derives locally scaled triplet translations from Linear Global Translation (LiGT) constraints and recovers global translations using weighted least squares. Synthetic and real-world experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and efficiency of the proposed methods.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: InfCoiL: Coordinated Planner-Controller Learning for Closed-Loop Physics-Based Human-Object Interaction
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yude Zou, Yifei Yao, Yiwei Hao, Hanqing Wang, Xing Gao
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: InfCoiL introduces a closed-loop framework for human-object interaction that integrates a morphology-aware planner and a multi-morphology controller, enhancing performance through coordinated learning and reinforcement.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Text- and goal-conditioned human-object interaction (HOI) provides an intuitive interface for specifying high-level intents in physics-based character animation. Mapping such intents to physically plausible, contact-rich behaviors naturally calls for a generative planner and a physics-based controller, yet existing planner-controller systems either execute plans open-loop or close the loop while keeping the planner fixed, so execution feedback never reshapes what is planned. We present InfCoiL, a closed-loop framework for physics-based HOI from coordinated planner-controller learning. InfCoiL couples a morphology-aware flow-matching planner with a unified multi-morphology controller through a shared morphology interface in an autoregressive plan-and-execute loop, and alternately fine-tunes both components with reinforcement learning from the same physical rollouts. To optimize the flow-matching planner online, we introduce Semantic Flow Policy Optimization (SFPO), which stochasticizes selected denoising transitions with channel-wise semantic covariance over heterogeneous HOI features and assigns group-relative, sequence-level rewards from complete closed-loop executions. On held-out OMOMO sequences, InfCoiL outperforms open-loop hierarchical baselines in goal-reaching task success and physical tracking accuracy. Project page: https://infcoil.github.io/

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yifei Yao, Yude Zou, Xing Gao, Guanbo Jiao, Yukai Wang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper introduces SimplEvo, a memory evolution framework for embodied agents that enhances performance without weight updates, achieving significant success rate improvements in task execution.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Efficient VLA Inference via Retrieval-Based Speculation and Hardware Acceleration
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zhengyang Cheng, He Zhu, Zeyu Guo, Zihan Liu, Anbang Wu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Zora is a hardware-software framework that accelerates vision-language-action inference by utilizing a lightweight retrieval model and optimizing action verification, achieving significant speedups on edge platforms.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to understand and execute complex instructions, but their autoregressive (AR) action generation introduces significant latency on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Speculative decoding can accelerate AR-based inference by parallelizing action generation and verification; however, existing approaches rely on costly draft models, which are inefficient on edge platforms. In this paper, we propose Zora, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference. Specifically, Zora introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models. We further reduce batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism. To address the retrieval overhead introduced by RAG-based drafting, we co-design dedicated hardware support, Zora core, to address the memory irregularity in RAG-based drafting. We evaluate Zora on four VLA models with the LIBERO benchmark. Zora retains comparable accuracy while achieving up to 3.4$\times$ speedup with software-only optimization and up to 7.6$\times$ speedup with hardware support over GPUs.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: WARP-JEPA: World-Model-in-the-Loop Amortized Rollout Planning for Frozen Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Junjie Li, Zhaojiacheng Zhou, Kaixiang Wang, Zihan Wang, QingSong Zhao
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: WARP-JEPA enhances long-horizon visual control by replacing costly gradient descent with efficient learned trajectory proposers, achieving significant speed and success improvements in planning.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Hierarchical Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (H-JEPA) enable long-horizon visual control but rely on costly test-time gradient descent for planning. Our analysis reveals that iterative optimization consumes up to 97.7% of episode runtime and that low predicted rollout costs do not necessarily translate into successful control. We further identify a planning-horizon asymmetry between long-horizon top-level composition and short two-step subordinate planning. To address these challenges, we propose WARP-JEPA, a hierarchical amortized planning framework that replaces online gradient optimization with learned multi-candidate trajectory proposers while keeping the world models frozen. WARP-JEPA combines a lightweight world-model-in-the-loop causal Transformer at the top level with parallel residual MLPs at subordinate levels. The proposers are trained using model-based rollout costs and best-of-K behavior cloning, enabling efficient candidate selection without test-time gradient optimization. Across 30 frozen H-JEPA models on four benchmarks, WARP-JEPA achieves 9.6-18.8x faster episode inference on long-horizon tasks (2.9-3.0x on Cube) and improves task success by up to 33.3 percentage points. These results demonstrate that amortized planning can substantially improve both inference efficiency and control performance without retraining the world models. Code is available at https://github.com/hideinsewer/WARP-JEPA.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Tac-DINO: Learning Tactile Features with Patch Alignment
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Hong Li, Yankang Dong, Yue Xu, Yihan Tang, Jiamin Qiu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Tac-DINO introduces a novel dataset and learning framework that enhances tactile perception in robotic manipulation through improved patch-level alignment and geometric supervision.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Multisensory perception is essential for robotic manipulation, with tactile sensing providing critical information for fine-grained, contact-rich interactions. Although prior work integrates tactile and spatial signals to improve perception, vision-tactile learning commonly relies on object-level alignment. Addressing this limitation requires systematically aligned 3D vision-tactile data. We develop a data collection system and introduce Touch3D, a dataset comprising 505 real-world objects and 20,025 tactile contacts. Building on this dataset, we establish the Contact-Centric Multimodal Tactile Representation Benchmark (CoMT-Bench), which expands evaluation from object-level retrieval and tactile properties to include patch-level contact evaluation. We further propose Geometry-Relation Distilled Tactile-Centric Cross-Modal Learning (GeoTAC), which explores tactile learning across all multisensory data. In experiments on the Touch3D test set, patch-level alignment improves the average score by 5.32 over object-level alignment, with GeoTAC's geometric supervision improving it by a further 4.48. In robotic manipulation, GeoTAC improves TP by 19.14 and 11.34 over DINOv2 (Vision-only) and DINOv2 (Vision-Tactile), respectively. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/tacdino.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: LSRP*: Scalable and Anytime Planning for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Asynchronous Actions
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Dachuan Liu, Shuai Zhou, Shizhe Zhao, Zhongqiang Ren
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: LSRP* is an improved anytime planner for Multi-Agent Path Finding that enhances solution quality and scalability, accommodating more agents and reducing costs compared to LSRP.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their respective starting locations to their respective goal locations while minimizing path costs. Although many MAPF algorithms were developed, most of them rely on a common assumption on synchronized actions, where the actions of all agents start at the same time and always take a time unit. This assumption may limit the use of MAPF planners in practice. To get rid of this assumption, recently, an algorithm called Loosely Synchronized Rule-based Planning (LSRP) was proposed, which can find sub-optimal solutions for many agents. However, LSRP often finds poor quality solutions due to its unbounded sub-optimality. This paper develops a new anytime planner called LSRP* that can keep improving solution quality after the initial solution is obtained until the runtime budget depletes. We analyze the properties of LSRP* and test it against several baselines with up to 1000 agents on various maps. LSRP* can handle up to 25% more agents than LSRP and can reduce up to 40% of the solution cost found by LSRP.

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).title: SurgTAP-3D: A Large-Scale Cross-Surgery Video Dataset with Contact-Aware 3D Motion Tracking
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Jiaxin Guo, Wenzhen Dong, Taoyu Wu, Haomin Kuang, Mengya Xu
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: SurgTAP-3D is a comprehensive dataset for 3D motion tracking in minimally invasive surgery, addressing tool-tissue interactions and enhancing autonomous surgical system development.
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).debug_abstract: Understanding 3D scene dynamics in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is a fundamental step toward physically intelligent and autonomous surgical systems. However, existing public datasets offer limited scalability and diversity in real-world clinical scenarios. Moreover, annotations typically focus on either tissue or instruments alone, overlooking tool-tissue interactions. This gap limits applications such as augmented reality guidance and autonomous surgery driven by vision-language-action (VLA) models or world models, which demand large-scale, high-quality 3D supervision. In this work, we construct SurgTAP-3D, a large-scale in-vivo pseudo-3D surgical motion tracking dataset and benchmark, comprising 520K frames, 4,549 action clips, and 1.4M 2D/3D point trajectories from diverse robotic and manual procedures under unified action categories. To make annotation scalable, we design a unified framework for surgical 3D point tracking that converts uncalibrated monocular surgical videos into structured 4D annotations through contact-region prompting, active-tool segmentation, dynamic bundle adjustment, and global 4D refinement. This pipeline adapts foundation priors to surgical videos and produces temporally consistent trajectories, pseudo-scale geometry, camera poses, and instrument masks. The dataset captures realistic challenges inherent to surgical environments, including occlusions, smoke, bleeding, and rapid instrument motion. We establish a comprehensive benchmark on SurgPose, SurgT, and STIR, covering both instrument and tissue tracking. We demonstrate instrument displacement estimation, deformable surface reconstruction, and foundation-model fine-tuning. Extensive experiments and analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset and annotation framework for 3D surgical point tracking, reconstruction, and surgical action understanding. Homepage: https://wrld.github.io/surgtap-3d/

机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).authors_text: Ziyang Zeng, Tingyang Chen, Jia Deng, Qiyao Wang, Shuo Tang
机器视觉与智能学习实验室 (MVIG).summary: WorkFactory is a framework that transforms professional intents into executable tasks, enhancing agent training through improved task environment quality and scalable task construction.

However, missing or inconsistent task information can disrupt expert demonstrations, weakening the resulting supervision.
